Given the target project version is Python 3.6, this CVE does not apply.

statements.action_statement: We’ve reasoned not to port this fix due to the following: - The upstream patch doesn’t change behavior - The official Python patch only adds deprecation warnings; it does not prevent the potentially problematic decoding. The actual behavior change is deferred to a future Python version (3.15+).  - Upstream explicitly declined to backport to older versions for compatibility reasons. See [[https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/125346|https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/125346|https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/125346|https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/125346]] for more details.

Not affected: Upstream Python disputes CVE-2023-36632—the RecursionError occurs only when the legacy email.utils.parseaddr API is explicitly invoked on pathologically malformed input, and raising that exception is the module’s documented size‑limit behavior. Not affected—the flaw is in the bzip2 library (libbz2) through 1.0.6, not in CPython itself. Python exposure was limited to historical Windows builds that bundled bzip2; Linux builds of Python 3.9 link dynamically to the system libbz2, so any remediation pertains to the OS bzip2 package rather than the Python project. Consequently, the Python 3.9 project is not impacted in this Linux server/VM context.
